debutant.question: In which city was Jesus born?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea (Matthew 2:1).

debutant.question: How many apostles did Jesus choose?
debutant.explanation: Jesus chose 12 apostles (Matthew 10:1-4).

debutant.question: Which apostle denied Jesus three times?
debutant.explanation: Peter denied Jesus three times before the rooster crowed (Matthew 26:34).

debutant.question: What is Jesus' first miracle?
debutant.explanation: Jesus' first miracle was changing water into wine at the wedding in Cana (John 2:1-11).

debutant.question: Who baptized Jesus?
debutant.explanation: John the Baptist baptized Jesus in the Jordan River (Matthew 3:13-17).

debutant.question: What is the last book of the New Testament?
debutant.explanation: Revelation (Revelation) is the last book of the New Testament.

debutant.question: How many days did Jesus spend in the desert?
debutant.explanation: Jesus spent 40 days and 40 nights in the desert (Matthew 4:2).

debutant.question: How many loaves did Jesus use to feed 5000 people?
debutant.explanation: Jesus used 5 loaves and 2 fish to feed the crowd (John 6:9).

debutant.question: In which gospel do we find the parable of the prodigal son?
debutant.explanation: The parable of the prodigal son is found only in the Gospel of Luke (Luke 15:11-32).

debutant.question: What is the name of Jesus' mother?
debutant.explanation: Mary is the mother of Jesus (Luke 1:27).

debutant.question: Where was Jesus crucified?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was crucified at Golgotha, 'place of the skull' (John 19:17).

debutant.question: How many days after his death did Jesus resurrect?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was resurrected on the third day (1 Corinthians 15:4).

debutant.question: Which apostle was a tax collector?
debutant.explanation: Matthew (Levi) was a tax collector before following Jesus (Matthew 9:9).

debutant.question: How many gospels are there in the New Testament?
debutant.explanation: There are 4 gospels: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

debutant.question: Who wrote the most New Testament epistles?
debutant.explanation: The apostle Paul wrote 13 epistles of the New Testament.

debutant.question: What does the dove that descended on Jesus during his baptism represent?
options: The soul of John the Baptist
debutant.explanation: The dove represents the Holy Spirit descending on Jesus at his baptism (Matthew 3:16).

debutant.question: What event is celebrated by Christians at Easter?
debutant.explanation: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ on the third day after his crucifixion.

debutant.question: What prayer did Jesus teach his disciples?
options: The prayer of the High Priest
debutant.explanation: Jesus taught the 'Our Father' to his disciples (Matthew 6:9-13).

debutant.question: Where was Jesus tempted by Satan?
options: On the banks of the Jordan
debutant.explanation: Jesus was tempted by Satan for 40 days in the wilderness (Matthew 4:1).

debutant.question: What is the main commandment that Jesus gives in John 13?
debutant.explanation: Jesus said 'Love one another, as I have loved you' (John 13:34).

debutant.question: In which town did Jesus grow up?
debutant.explanation: Jesus grew up in Nazareth of Galilee (Luke 2:51).

debutant.question: What was the profession of Joseph, father of Jesus?
debutant.explanation: Joseph was a carpenter (Matthew 13:55).

debutant.question: Which tree did Zacchaeus climb to see Jesus?
debutant.explanation: Zacchaeus, small in stature, had climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus passing by (Luke 19:4).

debutant.question: How many days after his resurrection did Jesus ascend to heaven?
debutant.explanation: Jesus ascended to heaven 40 days after his resurrection (Acts 1:3).

debutant.question: What is Pentecost celebrated in the Acts of the Apostles?
options: The descent of the Holy Spirit on the disciples
The birth of the Catholic Church
debutant.explanation: Pentecost is the descent of the Holy Spirit on the disciples gathered in Jerusalem, 50 days after Easter (Acts 2).

debutant.question: What was the birth name of the Apostle Paul?
debutant.explanation: Paul's name was Saul of Tarsus before his conversion on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:1).

debutant.question: How many books are in the New Testament?
debutant.explanation: The New Testament contains 27 books.

debutant.question: What miracle did Jesus perform on his friend Lazarus?
debutant.explanation: Jesus resurrected Lazarus 4 days after his death in Bethany (John 11:43-44).

debutant.question: What title does Jesus most often use to refer to himself?
debutant.explanation: Jesus refers to himself most often as 'Son of Man' (more than 80 times in the gospels).

debutant.question: Which NT book describes Paul's missionary journeys?
debutant.explanation: The Acts of the Apostles describe Paul's 3 missionary journeys and the birth of the first Churches.

debutant.question: What is the meaning of the word 'gospel'?
debutant.explanation: The word 'gospel' comes from the Greek 'euangelion' meaning 'good news'.

debutant.question: In which gospel is the Sermon on the Mount found?
debutant.explanation: The Sermon on the Mount, including the Beatitudes and the Lord's Prayer, is found in Matthew 5-7.

debutant.question: Which apostle wrote Revelation?
debutant.explanation: Revelation was written by John on the island of Patmos (Revelation 1:1,9).

debutant.question: Which NT character sought Jesus at night for a talk about the new birth?
debutant.explanation: Nicodemus, leader of the Pharisees, came to Jesus at night to discuss the Kingdom of God (John 3:1-2).

debutant.question: What is the meaning of the word 'Christ'?
debutant.explanation: 'Christ' comes from the Greek 'Christos' meaning 'anointed', equivalent to the Hebrew word 'Messiah'.

debutant.question: What Jewish holiday did Jesus celebrate at the Last Supper?
debutant.explanation: The Last Supper was a Passover meal that Jesus celebrated with his disciples (Matthew 26:17-20).

debutant.question: What city was the center of Jesus' ministry in Galilee?
debutant.explanation: Capernaum was the base of Jesus' Galilean ministry, called 'his own city' (Matthew 9:1).

debutant.question: Which disciple of Jesus was a doctor?
debutant.explanation: Luke was a physician ('the beloved physician', Colossians 4:14) and wrote the Gospel of Luke and Acts.

debutant.question: What parable does Jesus tell to describe the different types of hearts receiving the Word?
debutant.explanation: The parable of the sower describes 4 types of ground/heart receiving God's Word differently (Matthew 13:1-23).

debutant.question: What name does Jesus give to Simon after his confession of faith?
debutant.explanation: Jesus said to Simon 'You are Peter (Kephas), and on this rock I will build my Church' (Matthew 16:18).

debutant.question: What is the central message of the Gospel?
options: Jesus died and rose again for our sins
debutant.explanation: The gospel is that Jesus Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again (1 Corinthians 15:3-4).

debutant.question: Who was Pontius Pilate in the Passion of Jesus?
options: The High Priest who judged Jesus
The Roman governor who sentenced Jesus to death
debutant.explanation: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea who, although recognizing Jesus' innocence, condemned him to crucifixion (John 18:38; 19:16).

debutant.question: What symbol does Jesus use in John 15 to describe his relationship with believers?
debutant.explanation: Jesus said 'I am the vine, you are the branches' (John 15:5).

debutant.question: What is the meaning of 'Emmanuel'?
debutant.explanation: 'Immanuel' means 'God with us' (Matthew 1:23, quoting Isaiah 7:14).

debutant.question: Which country did Jesus visit as a refugee as a child?
debutant.explanation: Joseph, Mary, and the baby Jesus fled to Egypt to escape Herod's massacre (Matthew 2:13-15).

debutant.question: Which apostle wrote two NT epistles and was married?
debutant.explanation: Peter wrote two epistles (1 and 2 Peter) and was married (Matthew 8:14 mentions his mother-in-law).

debutant.question: What does the term 'apostle' mean?
options: Sent (one who is sent on a mission)
debutant.explanation: 'Apostle' comes from the Greek 'apostolos' meaning 'one who is sent'.

debutant.question: How many missionary journeys did Paul complete according to Acts?
debutant.explanation: Acts describes 3 major missionary journeys of Paul (Acts 13-14; 15-18; 18-21).

debutant.question: What does 'Pentecost' literally mean in Greek?
debutant.explanation: Pentecost comes from the Greek 'pentêkostê' meaning 'fiftieth' (Acts 2:1).

debutant.question: Which disciple asked Jesus to show him the way to the Father?
debutant.explanation: Philip said to Jesus, 'Lord, show us the Father.' Jesus responds: 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:8-9).

debutant.question: Which episode shows Jesus as a child in the Temple in Jerusalem?
options: Jesus among the doctors at age 12
debutant.explanation: At age 12, Jesus remained in the Temple in Jerusalem among the doctors of the Law (Luke 2:41-50).

debutant.question: What are the names of the four evangelists?
debutant.explanation: The four canonical Gospels bear the names Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

debutant.question: What did Mary lay the baby Jesus in when he was born?
debutant.explanation: There was no room for them in the inn, so Mary laid him in a manger (Luke 2:7).

debutant.question: Who were the first to come and worship the newborn Jesus on the night of his birth?
debutant.explanation: An angel announced the good news to the shepherds tending their flocks in the fields near Bethlehem (Luke 2:8-16).

debutant.question: What three gifts did the wise men of the East offer to the child Jesus?
debutant.explanation: The wise men opened their treasures and offered him gold, frankincense and myrrh (Matthew 2:11).

debutant.question: How many fish did Jesus use with the five loaves to feed the 5,000 men?
debutant.explanation: A young boy had five barley loaves and two fish, which Jesus multiplied for the crowd (John 6:9-13).

debutant.question: How many baskets full of remaining pieces were collected after the multiplication of the 5 loaves?
debutant.explanation: Twelve baskets were filled with the remaining pieces of the five barley loaves (John 6:13).

debutant.question: What miracle did Jesus perform on Lake Galilee when a great storm threatened the boat?
options: He threatened the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm
debutant.explanation: Jesus said to the sea: 'Silence! shut up !' and the wind ceased, causing the disciples to marvel (Mark 4:39-41).

debutant.question: How many lepers did Jesus heal when only one came back to thank him?
debutant.explanation: Ten lepers were cleansed by going to show themselves to the priests, but only one Samaritan returned to give glory to God (Luke 17:12-19).

debutant.question: Who carried the cross of Jesus on the way to Golgotha?
debutant.explanation: The soldiers commandeered Simon of Cyrene, who was returning from the fields, to carry the cross behind Jesus (Luke 23:26).

debutant.question: Whereupon did Jesus enter triumphantly into Jerusalem before the crowds shouting 'Hosanna'?
debutant.explanation: Jesus rode on a colt on which no one had yet sat, fulfilling Zechariah 9:9 (Mark 11:2-10).

debutant.question: What did the disciples do at the Last Supper with the bread and the cup?
options: They celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles
Jesus instituted the Lord's Supper ('This is my body... This is my blood')
debutant.explanation: At the last Passover meal, Jesus broke the bread and shared the cup in memorial of his death for the new covenant (Luke 22:19-20).

debutant.question: What gesture of humility does Jesus perform for his disciples before the Last Supper in John 13?
debutant.explanation: Jesus girded himself with a cloth and washed his disciples' feet to leave them an example of mutual service (John 13:4-15).

debutant.question: Which disciple cut off the ear of the high priest's servant when Jesus was arrested?
debutant.explanation: According to John 18:10, Simon Peter drew his sword and cut off Malchus's right ear, which Jesus immediately healed (Luke 22:51).

debutant.question: How did Judas Iscariot point out Jesus to the soldiers in the garden of Gethsemane?
debutant.explanation: Judas had given this sign: 'He whom I will kiss is him; take hold of it’ (Matthew 26:48-49).

debutant.question: Who was released by Pontius Pilate in place of Jesus at the request of the crowd?
debutant.explanation: Pilate released Barabbas, a bandit imprisoned for sedition and murder, and handed Jesus over to be crucified (Luke 23:18-25).

debutant.question: What inscription did Pilate place above Jesus' head on the cross?
options: Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews (INRI)
debutant.explanation: The sign read in Hebrew, Latin and Greek: 'Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews' (John 19:19-20).

debutant.question: To whom did Jesus entrust his mother Mary from the cross?
debutant.explanation: Jesus said to his mother, 'Woman, behold your son,' then to the disciple, 'Behold your mother' (John 19:26-27).

debutant.question: What did Jesus promise to the repentant thief crucified next to him?
options: That he would be released the next day
'Today you will be with me in paradise'
That he would become an apostle
That he would return to Nazareth
debutant.explanation: In response to the evildoer's faith ("Remember me"), Jesus assured him of immediate salvation (Luke 23:42-43).

debutant.question: Who asked Pilate for the body of Jesus to bury in a new tomb?
debutant.explanation: Joseph of Arimathea, a member of the Sanhedrin and secret disciple, placed the body of Jesus in his new tomb (John 19:38-42).

debutant.question: In the parable of the ten virgins (Matthew 25), what had the five foolish virgins forgotten?
options: To take oil in reserve for their lamps
debutant.explanation: The five wise virgins had taken oil in vessels with their lamps, ready for the bridegroom's arrival (Matthew 25:1-13).

debutant.question: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who finally stopped to help the man injured by the bandits?
debutant.explanation: When the priest and the Levite passed on, the Samaritan had compassion, bound up his wounds, and paid for his accommodation (Luke 10:30-37).

debutant.question: In the parable of the prodigal son, what did the father do when he saw his son returning from afar?
options: He ran and threw himself on her neck and kissed her
He asked her to repay the money
He made him work as a slave
debutant.explanation: Moved with compassion, the father ran to meet him, gave him the most beautiful robe, a ring and had the fatted calf killed (Luke 15:20-24).

debutant.question: In the parable of the lost sheep (Luke 15), how many sheep does the shepherd leave behind to search for the lost one?
debutant.explanation: The good shepherd leaves the other 99 in the wilderness to search for the one lost sheep until he finds it (Luke 15:4).

debutant.question: On what does the wise man build his house according to the end of the Sermon on the Mount?
debutant.explanation: He who hears the words of Jesus and puts them into practice is like a prudent man who built his house on a rock (Matthew 7:24).

debutant.question: What are the famous first words of the Beatitudes in Matthew 5?
options: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven
debutant.explanation: Jesus opens the Sermon on the Mount with nine beatitudes that overturn the values ​​of the world (Matthew 5:3-12).

debutant.question: What appeared above the heads of the disciples on the day of Pentecost?
debutant.explanation: Tongues of fire rested on each of them, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:3-4).

debutant.question: How many people were baptized on the day of Pentecost after Peter's preaching?
debutant.explanation: That day the number of disciples increased by about three thousand souls (Acts 2:41).

debutant.question: What miracle did Peter and John perform before the gate of the Temple called Beauty?
options: They healed a man lame from birth
debutant.explanation: Peter said to the lame man: 'I have neither silver nor gold; but what I have I give to you: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, arise and walk!' (Acts 3:6).

debutant.question: Which officer of a queen of Ethiopia was baptized by Philip after reading the prophet Isaiah in his chariot?
debutant.explanation: Philip announced Jesus to him from Isaiah 53, then baptized him in water on the road to Gaza (Acts 8:27-39).

debutant.question: How was the apostle Peter miraculously delivered from Herod's prison in Acts 12?
options: An angel of the Lord woke him up, removed his chains and opened the iron door
debutant.explanation: As the Church prayed continually for him, an angel led him out of the prison to Mary's house (Acts 12:7-17).

debutant.question: What did the jailer of Philippi ask Paul and Silas after the nighttime earthquake?
options: 'Lords, what must I do to be saved?'
debutant.explanation: Paul and Silas answered him, 'Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you and your family will be saved' (Acts 16:30-31).

debutant.question: Which New Testament epistle contains the famous 'hymn to love' (chapter 13)?
debutant.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13 exalts love (agape) as superior to all spiritual gifts.

debutant.question: Which New Testament epistle describes 'all the weapons of God' (armor of the believer) in chapter 6?
debutant.explanation: Ephesians 6:10-18 describes the belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit.

debutant.question: In James 2, what famous comparison does the author use to show that faith must be translated into action?
debutant.explanation: James teaches that genuine faith necessarily produces works of love and obedience (James 2:17,26).

debutant.question: Which book in the New Testament is called the 'heroes of the faith chapter' (in chapter 11)?
debutant.explanation: Hebrews 11 traces the faith of Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Moses, Rahab, David and the prophets.

debutant.question: In Revelation, what glorious title is written on the garment and thigh of the rider on the white horse (Rev 19:16)?
options: King of kings and Lord of lords
debutant.explanation: Revelation 19:16 proclaims the absolute sovereignty of the victorious Christ: 'King of kings and Lord of lords'.

debutant.question: Which young colleague did Paul call 'my true child in the faith'?
debutant.explanation: Paul shows deep fatherly affection for Timothy in 1 Timothy 1:2 and 2 Timothy 1:2.

debutant.question: What animal sang when Peter denied Jesus three times?
debutant.explanation: As soon as Peter denied the third time, the rooster crowed and Peter wept bitterly (Luke 22:60-62).

debutant.question: How many days did Jesus wait before going to Bethany after learning of Lazarus' illness?
options: He remained two more days where he was
debutant.explanation: Jesus stayed two more days so that the glory of God would shine through the resurrection of Lazarus on the 4th day (John 11:6,14-15).

debutant.question: Which blind man from Jericho cried out: 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' and regained his sight?
debutant.explanation: Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus, threw down his cloak, jumped to Jesus, and was healed by his faith (Mark 10:46-52).

debutant.question: What woman was healed of a twelve-year issue of blood by touching the hem of Jesus' garment?
debutant.explanation: Jesus said to her: 'My daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace’ (Mark 5:25-34).

debutant.question: What miracle did Jesus perform for the daughter of Jairus, leader of the synagogue?
options: He gave him back his sight
He raised her from the dead ('Talitha koumi')
debutant.explanation: Jesus took the hand of the twelve-year-old girl and said to her, 'Girl, get up!' (Mark 5:41-42).

debutant.question: Which short New Testament book is a personal letter from Paul to a Christian master on behalf of an escaped slave named Onesimus?
debutant.explanation: In the epistle to Philemon, Paul tenderly intercedes for Onesimus, who had become 'a beloved brother' (Philemon 1:16).

intermediaire.question: On which mountain was Jesus transfigured?
intermediaire.explanation: Tradition places the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor (Matthew 17:1-9).

intermediaire.question: Which NT character asked for the head of John the Baptist?
intermediaire.explanation: Herodias requested John the Baptist's head through his daughter (Mark 6:24-25).

intermediaire.question: In which book do we find Peter's speech at Pentecost?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter's speech at Pentecost is found in Acts 2.

intermediaire.question: Which NT woman poured perfume on Jesus' feet?
intermediaire.explanation: Mary of Bethany anointed Jesus' feet with expensive ointment (John 12:3).

intermediaire.question: What was Peter's job before following Jesus?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter was a fisherman on Lake Galilee (Matthew 4:18).

intermediaire.question: Which apostle walked on water toward Jesus?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter walked on water to join Jesus (Matthew 14:29).

intermediaire.question: What is the first epistle of Paul chronologically?
intermediaire.explanation: 1 Thessalonians is considered the oldest epistle of Paul (c. 50 AD).

intermediaire.question: Which book describes the vision of the new Jerusalem?
intermediaire.explanation: The New Jerusalem is described in Revelation 21.

intermediaire.question: Who said 'it is no longer I who live, it is Christ who lives in me'?
intermediaire.explanation: Paul writes this in Galatians 2:20.

intermediaire.question: Which NT woman was a purple merchant?
intermediaire.explanation: Lydia was a purple merchant from the city of Thyatira (Acts 16:14).

intermediaire.question: In which gospel does Jesus say 'I am the light of the world'?
intermediaire.explanation: It is in the Gospel of John that Jesus makes the statements 'I am...' (John 8:12).

intermediaire.question: Which disciple was chosen to replace Judas among the Twelve?
intermediaire.explanation: Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas (Acts 1:26).

intermediaire.question: Who is the first Christian martyr mentioned in Acts?
intermediaire.explanation: Stephen was the first Christian martyr, stoned to death after his speech before the Sanhedrin (Acts 7:59).

intermediaire.question: In which city were Paul and Silas imprisoned before an earthquake opened the gates?
intermediaire.explanation: In Philippi, an earthquake opened the prison doors (Acts 16:26).

intermediaire.question: What parable does Jesus tell to explain who our neighbor is?
options: The parable of the Good Samaritan
The Parable of the Lost Sheep
intermediaire.explanation: The parable of the Good Samaritan answers 'Who is my neighbor?' (Luke 10:25-37).

intermediaire.question: What event marks the beginning of the Church according to Acts?
intermediaire.explanation: Pentecost, with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, is the starting point of the Church (Acts 2).

intermediaire.question: What is special about the Gospel of John compared to the three synoptics?
options: It does not contain parables but revealing signs and speeches
He is the only one to mention the resurrection
intermediaire.explanation: John differs from the synoptics: no parables in the strict sense, but 7 miraculous 'signs' and 7 major 'I am' declarations revealing the divine identity of Jesus.

intermediaire.question: What theological concept does Paul mainly develop in the epistle to the Romans?
intermediaire.explanation: The book of Romans is the great exposition of justification by faith (Romans 1-8).

intermediaire.question: What is the main doctrine of the epistle to the Hebrews?
options: The superiority of the priesthood of Christ over the Levitical priesthood
intermediaire.explanation: The epistle to the Hebrews demonstrates the superiority of Christ as high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.

intermediaire.question: Which apostle refused to believe in the resurrection before seeing and touching Jesus?
intermediaire.explanation: Thomas said 'Except I see in his hands the mark of the nails...I will not believe' (John 20:25).

intermediaire.question: What was the main problem that Paul addresses in Galatians?
options: The false doctrine that circumcision and the Law of Moses were necessary for salvation
intermediaire.explanation: Paul fights in Galatians the 'Judaizers' who taught that faith in Christ was not enough.

intermediaire.question: What major decision did the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) make?
options: The list of canonical books of the NT
Gentiles do not need to be circumcised to be saved
The election of the first bishop of Rome
The ban on marriage for pastors
intermediaire.explanation: The Council of Jerusalem decided that Gentiles did not need to be circumcised to be saved (Acts 15).

intermediaire.question: What is the theological meaning of the term 'redemption' in the NT?
options: The Redemption of a Slave by the Payment of a Price — Christ has redeemed us by his blood
The moral transformation of the believer
intermediaire.explanation: Redemption (apolytrosis) literally means the redemption of a slave—Christ has redeemed us at a price (1 Corinthians 6:20).

intermediaire.question: What is the content of the hymn to Christ in Philippians 2:6-11 (kenosis)?
options: The voluntary abasement of Christ and his exaltation by God
intermediaire.explanation: The hymn of Philippians 2:6-11 describes kenosis: Christ 'emptied himself' by taking the form of a servant, and then God exalted him.

intermediaire.question: What is the main subject of the epistle of James?
intermediaire.explanation: James emphasizes that faith without works is dead (James 2:17).

intermediaire.question: What is the connection between the Lord's Supper and Passover in NT theology?
options: The Last Supper fulfills and replaces the Jewish Passover — Christ is the Passover Lamb
The Last Supper is entirely new with no connection to the OT
Passover and the Last Supper are unrelated parallel rites
intermediaire.explanation: Paul says 'Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed' (1 Corinthians 5:7). The Last Supper is the fulfillment of the Passover.

intermediaire.question: What Christological doctrine is condemned by John in his epistles (docetism)?
options: That Jesus was a simple man
That Jesus did not come in the flesh — denying the actual incarnation
That Jesus is inferior to the Father
intermediaire.explanation: Jean fights Docetism. 1 John 4:2: 'Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God.'

intermediaire.question: Which apostle was the first to recognize that the gospel extended to non-Jews (Gentiles)?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter received a vision of the cloth with unclean animals and was sent to the centurion Cornelius—the first baptism of a Gentile (Acts 10).

intermediaire.question: What is the difference between 'justification' and 'sanctification' in Pauline theology?
options: Justification is the legal act of God declaring us righteous; sanctification is the process of transformation in Christ
Justification comes from our works; the sanctification of faith
The justification is final; sanctification is impossible
intermediaire.explanation: Justification is an instantaneous act of God declaring the sinner righteous. Sanctification is the ongoing process of transformation.

intermediaire.question: What is the content of Jesus' great priestly prayer in John 17?
options: Prayer for healing of the sick
Prayer for the glory of the Father, the protection of the disciples and the unity of all believers
intermediaire.explanation: John 17: for his own glorification (v.1-5), for his disciples (v.6-19) and for all future believers (v.20-26).

intermediaire.question: Which NT text describes the 'fruit of the Spirit' in 9 characteristics?
intermediaire.explanation: Galatians 5:22-23 lists the 9 fruits of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.

intermediaire.question: What is the problem that Paul addresses in 1st Corinthians?
options: Divisions in the Church, Immorality, Misused Spiritual Gifts
intermediaire.explanation: 1 Corinthians addresses multiple issues: factions, immorality, marriage, sacrificed meat, worship and giving, resurrection.

intermediaire.question: What is the meaning of the term 'grace' (charis) in NT theology?
options: Unmerited divine favor freely granted by God for salvation
The moral beauty of the believer
intermediaire.explanation: 'Charis' is divine grace—the absolutely free and unmerited favor of God (Ephesians 2:8-9).

intermediaire.question: What is the central theme of the epistle to the Hebrews expressed by the repetition of 'best' (kreittôn)?
options: The superiority of the Church over Israel
The absolute superiority of Christ and the new covenant over all that has gone before
The superiority of the Jews over the Gentiles
The superiority of Paul over the other apostles
intermediaire.explanation: The Epistle to the Hebrews uses 'kreittôn' (better) 13 times: better name, better alliance, better promises, better sacrifice.

intermediaire.question: What is the unique contribution of Luke's gospel to NT theology?
options: Emphasis on the divinity of Christ
Emphasis on prayer, the Holy Spirit, women, the poor and the universal scope of salvation
intermediaire.explanation: Luke is distinguished by: the centrality of prayer, the Holy Spirit, the marginalized (women, poor, sinners, Samaritans, Gentiles).

intermediaire.question: What is the meaning of the term 'incarnation' in NT Christology?
options: The Eternal Son of God Taking Full Human Nature
The human appearance of God in the OT
intermediaire.explanation: The incarnation refers to the act by which the eternal Son of God took on a full human nature in John 1:14: 'The Word was made flesh.'

intermediaire.question: What is the relationship between 'law' and 'gospel' in Pauline theology?
options: Law and gospel are the same
The Law reveals sin and leads to Christ; the Gospel announces free grace
The Law replaces the Gospel in the NT
The Gospel completely abolishes the Law without remainder
intermediaire.explanation: Paul: 'The law is our teacher to bring us to Christ' (Galatians 3:24). The Law accuses, the Gospel liberates.

intermediaire.question: What is the meaning of the 'New Covenant' established by Jesus at the Last Supper?
options: The fulfillment of Jeremiah 31:31-34: forgiveness of sins, law in the hearts, direct access to God through the blood of Christ
The creation of a new religion separate from Judaism
A conditional covenant based on our obedience
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus said 'This cup is the new covenant in my blood' (Luke 22:20) — fulfilling the promise of Jeremiah 31:31-34.

intermediaire.question: What is the name of the high priest who presided over the religious trial of Jesus before the Sanhedrin?
intermediaire.explanation: Joseph Caiaphas, Annas' son-in-law, was high priest that year and declared that one man must die for the people (John 11:49-51; 18:13-24).

intermediaire.question: Which member of the Sanhedrin gave advice of prudence by saying that if the work of the apostles comes from God, it cannot be destroyed?
intermediaire.explanation: Gamaliel, a doctor of the Law esteemed by all the people (and teacher of Paul), recommended not to fight against God (Acts 5:34-39).

intermediaire.question: What was the name of the Christian couple who lied to the Holy Spirit about the price of a field sold in Acts 5?
intermediaire.explanation: Ananias and Sapphira kept part of the price while pretending they were giving it all; Peter exposed their lies before God (Acts 5:1-11).

intermediaire.question: How many deacons ('seven men of good testimony') were chosen in Acts 6 to wait tables?
intermediaire.explanation: The Church chose seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom, including Stephen and Philip, so that the apostles would devote themselves to prayer and the Word (Acts 6:3-6).

intermediaire.question: Which magician from Samaria wanted to buy from the apostles the power to confer the Holy Spirit?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter severely rebuked Simon, saying, 'Let your money perish with you!' (Acts 8:18-23), hence the word 'simony'.

intermediaire.question: Which Jewish prophet and magician in Cyprus opposed Paul before Sergius Paulus and was struck with temporary blindness?
intermediaire.explanation: Elymas the magician sought to turn the proconsul away from the faith; Paul rebuked him and a cloud darkened his eyes (Acts 13:8-11).

intermediaire.question: What young man fell asleep during Paul's long speech at Troas, fell from the third story, and was brought back to life?
intermediaire.explanation: Paul came down, leaned over Eutychus, took him in his arms and assured that his soul was in him (Acts 20:9-12).

intermediaire.question: Which Ephesian craftsman making silver temples of Artemis caused a riot in the theater against Paul?
intermediaire.explanation: Demetrius feared for the commerce and prestige of the temple of Artemis in the face of Christian conversions (Acts 19:24-29).

intermediaire.question: In which gospel does Jesus pronounce the seven great 'I am' with attributes (Bread of life, Light, Door, Good Shepherd, Resurrection, Way, True Vine)?
intermediaire.explanation: The Gospel of John structures its Christological revelation around these seven declarations 'Egô eimi'.

intermediaire.question: What is unique about the Gospel of Mark in terms of its style and length?
options: It is the longest and contains long speeches
It is the shortest and most dynamic ('immediately'), centered on the action and the cross of the Servant
It begins with a genealogy back to Adam
He doesn't tell of any miracles
intermediaire.explanation: Mark frequently uses 'euthys' ('at once'), presenting Jesus as the servant Son of God who gives his life as a ransom (Mark 10:45).

intermediaire.question: Why does the Gospel of Matthew begin with a genealogy going back to Abraham and David?
options: To prove that Jesus was Roman
To show Jewish readers that Jesus is the rightful heir of the promises made to Abraham and King David
To imitate the epistles of Paul
Because he didn't know about the virgin birth
intermediaire.explanation: Matthew 1:1-17 organizes 3 series of 14 generations culminating in Jesus the Messiah, son of David and son of Abraham.

intermediaire.question: Why does Luke's genealogy (chapter 3) go back to Adam and 'son of God'?
options: Because Luke only writes for the Pharisees
To underline the universal scope of Jesus' salvation for all humanity descended from Adam
To deny the covenant with Abraham
intermediaire.explanation: Luke highlights God's universal mercy towards the poor, women, Samaritans and all nations.

intermediaire.question: What song of praise did Mary sing during her visit to Elizabeth in Luke 1?
options: The Magnificat ('My soul exalts the Lord...')
intermediaire.explanation: The Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55) celebrates God's faithfulness in lifting up the humble and fulfilling his promise to Israel.

intermediaire.question: What song did Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, utter when his tongue was loosed (Luke 1:68-79)?
options: The Benedictus ('Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel...')
intermediaire.explanation: In the Benedictus, Zechariah blesses God for messianic deliverance and prophesies the preparatory mission of his son John.

intermediaire.question: What parable from the Gospel of Luke illustrates humility in prayer in the face of religious self-sufficiency?
options: The Pharisee and the publican (tax collector) at the Temple
intermediaire.explanation: The publican, not daring to lift his eyes, said: 'O God, be merciful to me, a sinner!' and went away justified (Luke 18:9-14).

intermediaire.question: What parable teaches perseverance in prayer in the face of an indifferent magistrate (Luke 18:1-8)?
options: The importunate widow and the unjust judge
intermediaire.explanation: If even an unjust judge ends up doing justice to a persevering widow, how much more will God hear his elect.

intermediaire.question: In Matthew 18:21-35, what parable does Jesus tell after telling Peter to forgive 'until seventy times seven'?
options: The merciless servant (who refuses to forgive a small debt after being forgiven of a huge debt)
intermediaire.explanation: The one to whom the king has given ten thousand talents refuses to wait for a hundred denarii, illustrating the demand for forgiveness received from God.

intermediaire.question: In the parable of the workers in the vineyard (Matthew 20:1-16), why do those first hired murmur?
options: Eleventh hour workers received the same denarius as them — illustrating God's sovereign and generous grace
intermediaire.explanation: 'Is your eye bad because I am good?' reminds us that salvation is a gracious gift and not a earned wage.

intermediaire.question: What night talk in John 3 exposes the need to be 'born again / from above' (of water and the Spirit)?
options: The interview with the Samaritan woman
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus explains to Nicodemus, doctor of Israel, that no one can enter the Kingdom of God without regeneration by the Spirit (John 3:3-8).

intermediaire.question: In John 4, what truth does Jesus reveal to the Samaritan woman about the true place of worship?
options: The hour is coming when true worshipers will worship the Father 'in spirit and in truth'
A third temple must be built in Nazareth
intermediaire.explanation: God is Spirit: true worship no longer depends on a geographical sanctuary but on a heart renewed in truth (John 4:21-24).

intermediaire.question: In John 6, why did many of the disciples withdraw after the 'Bread of Life' talk?
options: Because there was no more bread
Because they were shocked by Jesus' demanding words ('eat his flesh and drink his blood', that is, fully believe in his life-giving death)
intermediaire.explanation: To Jesus' question: 'And you, do you not also want to go?', Peter replied: 'Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life' (John 6:68).

intermediaire.question: In 1 Corinthians 15, what event does Paul present as the essential foundation without which the Christian faith would be in vain?
options: The bodily resurrection of Christ and the future resurrection of believers
intermediaire.explanation: 'Unless Christ is raised, your faith is in vain; you are still in your sins' (1 Corinthians 15:17).

intermediaire.question: According to 1 Corinthians 15:6, to how many brothers did the resurrected Jesus appear at one time before Paul's epistle?
options: To more than 500 brothers at a time
intermediaire.explanation: Paul specifies that most of these more than 500 witnesses were still alive at the time of his writing (~55 AD).

intermediaire.question: In 2 Corinthians 5:18-20, what title does Paul give to believers who proclaim reconciliation with God?
intermediaire.explanation: 'We therefore act as ambassadors for Christ, as if God were exhorting through us: Be ye reconciled to God!'

intermediaire.question: In 2 Corinthians 12:7-9, what response did the Lord give to Paul who prayed three times to be delivered from his 'thorn in the flesh'?
options: 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness'
He told him to go to Jerusalem
He ordered her to be quiet
intermediaire.explanation: Paul thus learns to glory even in his weaknesses so that the power of Christ rests on him.

intermediaire.question: In Romans 5:12-21, what major typological parallel does Paul draw to explain the fall and salvation?
options: Between the first Adam (disobedience, sin, death) and Jesus Christ, the new/last Adam (obedience, grace, life)
intermediaire.explanation: Through the fault of one, condemnation has reached all men; by the righteous act of one life-giving justification is offered to all.

intermediaire.question: In Romans 8:1-17, what contrast structures the Christian life?
options: Living according to the flesh (which leads to death) vs walking according to the Spirit (which gives life, adoption and hope)
intermediaire.explanation: The Spirit of adoption makes us cry 'Abba! Father !' and testifies to our spirit that we are children and heirs of God.

intermediaire.question: In Romans 12:1, how does Paul define the 'reasonable/spiritual worship' of believers?
options: Offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God
intermediaire.explanation: In response to God's mercies (Romans 1-11), the believer's entire daily existence becomes a living offering.

intermediaire.question: In Galatians 3:24, to what ancient role does Paul compare the Law of Moses before the coming of faith?
options: A teacher (tutor/guide) who led us to Christ
intermediaire.explanation: The 'paidagogos' in the Greco-Roman world escorted and supervised the child until he came of age; the coming of Christ inaugurates the age of sonship by faith.

intermediaire.question: In Galatians 3:28, what three social, religious, and cultural barriers are transcended 'in Christ Jesus'?
options: There is no longer Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female—all one in Christ Jesus
intermediaire.explanation: Without erasing created distinctions, the Gospel gives all believers equal dignity and equal access to salvation in Christ.

intermediaire.question: In Ephesians 2:8-10, what place do grace, faith and good works have respectively?
options: We are saved by grace through faith (the gift of God, not by works), to do good works prepared in advance
intermediaire.explanation: Good works are not the root but the fruit of salvation freely received by grace.

intermediaire.question: In Philippians 3:7-8, how does Paul now view his former religious privileges (circumcision, blameless Pharisee)?
options: As loss and mire for the excellency of the knowledge of Jesus Christ
intermediaire.explanation: Paul renounces his own righteousness from the Law to receive the righteousness that comes from God through faith in Christ.

intermediaire.question: In Colossians 1:15-17, how does Paul describe the cosmic supremacy of Christ?
options: 'The image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation', by whom and for whom everything was created
intermediaire.explanation: This Christological hymn affirms that all things subsist in Christ and all fullness dwells in him (Colossians 1:19).

intermediaire.question: In 1 Thessalonians 5:1-6, to what image do Jesus and Paul compare the sudden coming of the Day of the Lord to the sleeping world?
options: A king announcing his journey a year before
intermediaire.explanation: This is why believers, 'children of light', are called to watch and be sober.

intermediaire.question: In 1 Timothy 2:5, how does Paul summarize the uniqueness of mediation between God and men?
options: 'There is one God, and also one mediator between God and men, the man Jesus Christ'
intermediaire.explanation: True God and true man, Jesus Christ is the only bridge between humanity and God, having given himself as a ransom for all.

intermediaire.question: In 2 Timothy 4:7, what three-fold metaphor does Paul use at the brink of his death to describe his faithfulness?
options: 'I fought the good fight, I finished the race, I kept the faith'
I have written a hundred books
intermediaire.explanation: Paul now confidently awaits the 'crown of righteousness' that the Lord, the righteous judge, will give him that day.

intermediaire.question: In Hebrews 4:14-16, what comfort do we take from Jesus being our 'great high priest'?
options: He was tempted in all things as we are, yet sinless—so we can approach the throne of grace with confidence.
intermediaire.explanation: The compassion of the glorified Christ opens to believers confident access to mercy and timely help.

intermediaire.question: In Hebrews 12:1-2, who is called 'the leader and finisher of the faith'?
intermediaire.explanation: Surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, believers fix their eyes on Jesus who endured the cross in view of the joy that was reserved for him.

intermediaire.question: In James 3:1-12, what does James compare the human tongue to despite its small size?
options: To the bit in the horse's mouth, to the rudder of the ship and to a small fire that sets a large forest ablaze
intermediaire.explanation: James emphasizes the immense power of words to bless or destroy, calling for mastery through wisdom from above.

intermediaire.question: In 1 Peter 2:9, what title from Exodus (19:6) does Peter apply to the entire Church?
options: A chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a acquired people
The servants of the Stone Temple
intermediaire.explanation: All believers form a royal priesthood called to announce the virtues of Him who called them from darkness to his admirable light.

intermediaire.question: In 1 John 1:8-9, what does John say if someone claims to have no sin?
options: We deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us; but if we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us
intermediaire.explanation: The Christian life is not based on the pretension of impeccability but on sincere confession and purification by the blood of Jesus.

intermediaire.question: In 1 John 4:1-3, what doctrinal test allows us to discern the Spirit of God from the spirit of antichrist?
options: Confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh
intermediaire.explanation: Against pre-Gnostic errors denying the real incarnation, John poses the confession of Jesus Christ come in the flesh as the decisive criterion.

intermediaire.question: In Revelation 1:9-20, where was the apostle John when he received the vision of Christ glorified in the midst of the seven golden lampstands?
options: On the island of Patmos, because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus
intermediaire.explanation: The seven golden candlesticks represent the seven Churches of Asia Minor, and the seven stars in his right hand their angels/messengers.

intermediaire.question: In Revelation 2-3, which Church is praised for its love, faith, and perseverance despite material poverty ("You are rich!")?
intermediaire.explanation: Smyrna endures persecution and poverty without receiving any reproach from Jesus, who promises him the crown of life (Revelation 2:8-11).

intermediaire.question: In Revelation 3:17, what severe rebuke does Christ address to the Church of Laodicea?
options: That she thinks she is rich and needs nothing, unaware that she is unhappy, miserable, poor, blind and naked
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus advises him to buy from him gold tested in the fire, white garments and eye salve to see clearly (Revelation 3:18).

intermediaire.question: In Revelation 5, who alone is found worthy to open the book sealed with seven seals?
options: The Lion of the tribe of Judah / the Lamb as slain
One of the twenty-four old men
intermediaire.explanation: Announced as the Lion of Judah, he appears in the form of a Lamb slain but standing, worthy by his redeeming blood (Revelation 5:5-9).

intermediaire.question: In Revelation 7:9, who makes up the 'great crowd that no one could number' before the throne?
options: People from every nation, tribe, people, and tongue, dressed in white robes
intermediaire.explanation: This vision fulfills the promise made to Abraham by showing the universal salvation celebrated in heaven.

intermediaire.question: In Luke 10:38-42, what lesson does Jesus give to Martha, agitated by many cares, while Mary listens at his feet?
options: That Mary chose 'the good part, which will not be taken away from her': listening to the Word of the Lord before any agitation
That Marthe must leave the house
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus does not oppose service and prayer, but recalls the absolute priority of attentive listening to his Word.

intermediaire.question: What miracle did Jesus perform on the Sabbath that angered the synagogue leaders in Luke 13:10-17?
options: He heals a woman who has been bent for eighteen years
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus reminded us that we untie our ox or donkey on the Sabbath: how much more so this daughter of Abraham who has been bound for 18 years!

intermediaire.question: In John 20:24-29, what blessedness does Jesus pronounce after Thomas confesses him 'My Lord and my God!' ?
options: 'Blessed are those who touch my wounds'
'Blessed are those who have not seen and believed!'
'Blessed are those who remain in Jerusalem'
intermediaire.explanation: This last beatitude of the Gospels speaks directly to all generations of believers who believe in the apostolic testimony.

intermediaire.question: In Luke 24:27, how did the resurrected Jesus enlighten the two disciples who were felled on the road to Emmaus?
options: By a vision of armed angels
Beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures what concerned himself
By showing them the Temple in ruins
intermediaire.explanation: The disciples' hearts burned within them as he opened the Scriptures to them, and then they recognized him when he broke the bread (Luke 24:30-32).

intermediaire.question: Which character in the book of Acts sold a field and brought the price at the feet of the apostles, receiving the nickname 'son of exhortation'?
intermediaire.explanation: Acts 4:36-37 presents Barnabas as a model of generosity and encouragement in the early Church.

intermediaire.question: In Acts 17:23, which Athenian altar did Paul use as a platform to announce the Creator God?
options: The altar inscribed 'To an unknown god'
intermediaire.explanation: Paul departed from this altar to proclaim the God who made the world, who does not dwell in temples made with hands and who will judge through the resurrected Christ.

intermediaire.question: In Romans 11:17-24, what horticultural image does Paul use to explain the integration of Gentile believers into God's people?
options: Wild olive branches grafted onto the olive tree (Israel) to contribute to its sap
intermediaire.explanation: This metaphor calls Gentile Christians to humility and recognition of Israel's patriarchal roots.

intermediaire.question: In 1 Corinthians 12, what does Paul compare the Church and the diversity of spiritual gifts to?
options: To a single body composed of several members having different functions but all essential
intermediaire.explanation: The eye cannot say to the hand 'I have no need of you': the same Spirit distributes gifts for the common good (1 Corinthians 12:7-27).

expert.question: What Greek term refers to the second coming of Christ in the epistles?
expert.explanation: The Greek term 'Parousia' (παρουσία) refers to the second coming of Christ (1 Thessalonians 4:15).

expert.question: In Revelation 2-3, how many churches does Jesus address?
expert.explanation: Jesus addresses his messages to 7 Churches in Asia Minor (Revelation 2-3).

expert.question: What Pauline theological term means 'reconciliation by substitution'?
expert.explanation: 'Propitation' (ἱλαστήριον) refers to the act which appeases God's righteous wrath (Romans 3:25).

expert.question: According to Paul in Ephesians, what is the Church founded on?
options: Apostles and prophets, with Christ as the cornerstone
expert.explanation: The Church is founded on the apostles and prophets, with Christ being the cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20).

expert.question: In John 1, what Greek term is translated 'Word'?
expert.explanation: John uses 'Logos' (λόγος) to refer to Christ (John 1:1).

expert.question: Which city is cryptically referred to as 'Babylon' in 1 Peter 5:13?
expert.explanation: Historians agree that 'Babylon' in 1 Peter 5:13 refers to Rome.

expert.question: In Hebrews 7, to what priestly order is the priesthood of Christ compared?
expert.explanation: Christ is declared 'high priest according to the order of Melchizedek' (Hebrews 7:17).

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'Abba' in Romans 8:15?
expert.explanation: 'Abba' is the affectionate Aramaic term for 'Father', equivalent to 'Daddy'.

expert.question: In Revelation, what is the number of the 'Beast'?
expert.explanation: The number of the Beast is 666 (Revelation 13:18).

expert.question: What doctrine affirms that the two natures of Christ coexist without mixture or confusion?
expert.explanation: The Council of Chalcedon (451) defined the two complete natures of Christ.

expert.question: On which hill did Paul deliver his speech to the Athenians (Acts 17)?
expert.explanation: Paul delivered his speech on the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17:22).

expert.question: What NT Greek term describes the gathering of the Christian Church?
expert.explanation: 'Ekklesia' (ἐκκλησία) means 'assembly of the called out'.

expert.question: In Pauline theology, what is 'justification by faith' (dikaiôsis)?
options: A divine legal act by which the sinner is declared righteous
expert.explanation: For Paul, justification is a legal act (forensic) by which God declares the sinner righteous on the basis of faith in Christ.

expert.question: What central Johannine concept describes the 'dwelling' of Christ in the believer?
expert.explanation: The verb 'menein' (μένειν, remain) is central in John 15:4-7 and 1 John 4:16.

expert.question: What hypothetical source designates the material common to Matthew and Luke, absent from Mark?
expert.explanation: The 'Q source' (from the German Quelle = source) is a hypothetical source of Jesus' sayings.

expert.question: What is the main issue of the 'synoptic problem' in biblical theology?
options: Why there are 4 gospels and not just one
How to explain the similarities and differences between Matthew, Mark and Luke
The authenticity of the gospel of John
The date of composition of the gospels
expert.explanation: The 'synoptic problem' deals with the literary dependence between Matthew, Mark and Luke.

expert.question: What is the theological meaning of the term 'atonement' (hilasmos) in 1 John 2:2?
options: The act by which Christ satisfies divine justice and appeases the wrath of God for our sins
expert.explanation: 'Hilasmos' means 'propitiation' — the act by which Christ fulfills the requirements of divine holiness (1 John 2:2; 4:10; Romans 3:25).

expert.question: What is the structure of Jesus' 'Apocalyptic Discourse' in Matthew 24-25?
options: A simple list of chronological signs
An answer to two questions (destruction of the Temple / sign of the Parousia) with a double prophetic perspective
An allegory on the life of the Church
expert.explanation: Matthew 24-25 answers the disciples' questions about the destruction of the Temple AND the final Parousia, intertwining the two horizons.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'kenosis' in Pauline Christology (Philippians 2:7)?
options: The self-emptying of the Son—he renounced the independent exercise of certain divine attributes by incarnating
expert.explanation: Kenosis (κένωσις): the Son of God 'emptied himself' (ekénôsen) by taking the form of a servant (Philippians 2:7).

expert.question: What is the difference between 'rhema' and 'logos' in the Greek NT?
options: 'Logos' means the immutable divine Word (John 1:1); 'rhemah' refers to a specific word spoken (Romans 10:17)
'Logos' is the NT, 'rhema' is the OT
'Logos' is the teaching, 'rhema' is the prophecy
expert.explanation: 'Logos' tends towards the overall divine Word, 'rhema' towards a specific spoken word. Romans 10:17: 'Faith comes by hearing.'

expert.question: What is the significance of the statement 'Before Abraham was, I Am' (John 8:58)?
options: A claim to absolute divine identity: the divine name 'I Am' (YHWH, Exodus 3:14) applies to Christ
A simple sign of spiritual greatness
expert.explanation: John 8:58: 'Ego eimi' refers directly to the divine name YHWH ('I am he who am', Exodus 3:14). The Jews seeking to stone him confirm that they understood the divine claim.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'metanoia' (repentance) in the gospels in relation to simple regret?
options: A radical change in mental, spiritual, and practical orientation—existential turn toward God
The simple admission of one's faults
expert.explanation: 'Metanoia' (meta = change + noein = think) designates a radical and total change of existential direction. John the Baptist and Jesus proclaim metanoia as a condition of entry into the Kingdom.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'propitiation' (hilastêrion) in Romans 3:25 and how it relates to the OT?
options: The 'mercy seat' or mercy seat of the Ark — Jesus is its fulfillment in his own person
A Greek philosophical term unrelated to the OT
expert.explanation: Romans 3:25 uses 'hilastêrion' — the same term as the LXX for the 'kapporeth' (cover of the Ark). God publicly presented Christ as THIS place of propitiation.

expert.question: What is the Trinitarian baptismal formula of Matthew 28:19 and its dogmatic significance?
options: Three separate baptisms for each divine person
A single baptism in a single Trinitarian 'Name' (singular) — testifying to the unity and tripersonality of God
A liturgical formula without dogmatic significance
expert.explanation: Matthew 28:19: 'in the name' (eis to onoma, singular) of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit - the singular 'name' testifies to the divine unity in the threefold personal distinction.

expert.question: What is the significance of the image of the 'Lamb of God' (John 1:29) in sacrificial theology?
options: Convergence between the Passover lamb (Exodus 12), the Suffering Servant (Isaiah 53:7), daily sacrifices and the Lamb of the Apocalypse
A reference to the scapegoat of Leviticus 16
expert.explanation: The image of the lamb in John 1:29 is a typological convergence: paschal lamb, Suffering Servant, daily sacrifice, and the Lamb of the Apocalypse.

expert.question: What is the meaning of 'telos' in Matthew 5:48 ('be ye perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect')?
options: 'Telos' = complete, accomplished, mature — call for maturity and integrity in love
A Platonic ideal of moral excellence
expert.explanation: 'Teleios' comes from 'telos' (goal, accomplishment) — not flawless perfection, but maturation and accomplished love. The context is about loving your enemies as God loves all.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the baptismal formula 'in the name of the Father, of the Son and of the Holy Spirit' in Trinitarian theology?
options: A single baptism in a single Trinitarian 'Name' (singular) — testifying to the unity and tripersonality of God
A liturgical formula without dogmatic significance
A post-apostolic development absent from the primitive NT
expert.explanation: Matthew 28:19: 'in the name' (singular) testifies to the divine unity in the threefold personal distinction. This verse is one of the foundations of the Trinitarian doctrine.

expert.question: What is the cosmic significance of the reconciliation in Colossians 1:20?
options: Only the reconciliation of human beings with God
The reconciliation of 'all things' — heaven and earth — through the blood of Christ
The apocatastasis (universal salvation of all beings)
The pacification of human conflicts only
expert.explanation: Colossians 1:20 states that God has purposed to 'reconcile all things to himself through Christ.' Redemption has cosmic significance.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the 'resurrection of the body' as a Christian hope distinct from the Platonic immortality of the soul?
options: Resurrection involves the rehabilitation of the whole person, body and soul; Platonic immortality frees the soul from the body
Resurrection is simply the survival of the soul
Resurrection is not taught in the NT consistently
expert.explanation: Christian resurrection involves the rehabilitation of the whole person. The body is not a prison but a good creation destined for glorious transformation (1 Corinthians 15:35-54).

expert.question: What is the meaning of 'mystery' (mustêrion) in Paul in Ephesians 3:6?
options: An esoteric secret reserved for initiates
What was hidden in ages past and now revealed: Gentile joint heirs with Israel in the one Body of Christ
expert.explanation: 'Mustêrion' in Paul designates a progressively accomplished divine revelation: 'the nations are joint heirs, members of the same body' (Ephesians 3:6).

expert.question: What is the theology of the Holy Spirit developed in John 14-16?
options: Spirit is a divine impersonal force
The Holy Spirit is the third divine person: Comforter, Spirit of truth, convicter of sin and righteousness
The Spirit is an intermediary angel
The Spirit is a metaphor for prophetic inspiration only
expert.explanation: John 14-16 reveals the Paraclete as a divine person: he teaches (14:26), testifies (15:26), convicts of sin (16:8), and glorifies Christ (16:14).

expert.question: What is the meaning of 'double imputation' in Reformed NT soteriology?
options: Two sins attributed to the same individual
The sin of all imputed to Christ, and the righteousness of Christ imputed to believers
Justification and sanctification as two separate acts
expert.explanation: Double imputation: (1) the sins of believers are imputed to Christ (2 Corinthians 5:21) and (2) the perfect righteousness of Christ is imputed to believers through faith (Romans 5:17).

expert.question: What is the meaning of the concept of 'union with Christ' (in Christô) which appears more than 160 times in Paul?
options: The mystical and real union of the believer with the person of the resurrected Christ, foundation of all Christian life
Conformity to the teachings of Jesus
expert.explanation: 'In Christô' (160+ occurrences): the mystical, vital and real union of the believer with the resurrected Christ - the basis of justification, sanctification, adoption and glorification.

expert.question: In the theology of John's Gospel, what does the phrase 'the hour of Jesus' mean (John 2:4; 12:23; 13:1; 17:1)?
options: The hour of his glorification by his death on the cross, his resurrection and his return to the Father
The time of the destruction of Rome
expert.explanation: In John, the cross is not a defeat followed by glory, but the very place where the Son is 'lifted up' and glorified (John 12:23-33).

expert.question: What is the 'messianic secret' identified by exegetes in the Gospel of Mark?
options: Jesus' repeated injunctions to the demons, the healed, and the disciples not to disclose his identity as Messiah before the cross and resurrection
expert.explanation: Jesus avoids the misunderstandings of a triumphalist nationalist messianism until his identity is revealed at the cross (Mark 8:30; 15:39).

expert.question: What is the significance of the Roman centurion's confession at the foot of the cross in Mark 15:39 ('Truly this man was the Son of God!')?
options: Mark's Literary and Theological Summit: A Pagan Recognizes Jesus' True Identity at the Exact Moment He Dies
expert.explanation: The Gospel which opened with 'Gospel of Jesus Christ, Son of God' (1:1) culminates in the mouth of a Roman centurion before the Crucified.

expert.question: In Matthew, what does it mean to group Jesus' teachings into five major discourses (ch. 5-7, 10, 13, 18, 24-25)?
options: A structuring parallel presenting Jesus as the new and greater Moses giving the Law of the Kingdom (like the 5 books of the Pentateuch)
expert.explanation: Each discourse ends with the phrase 'When Jesus had finished these discourses...' (Matthew 7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1).

expert.question: What Greek term used by Jesus in John 14:16 ('Parakletos') refers to the Holy Spirit?
expert.explanation: The Paraclete is the one who is called to the believer's side to assist him, teach him, testify and convince the world (John 14-16; 1 John 2:1 for Jesus).

expert.question: What is the distinction between 'kerygma' and 'didachè' in New Testament studies?
options: These are two cities in Greece
The kerygma is the central missionary proclamation of the death and resurrection of Christ; didache is the moral and doctrinal teaching given to believers
Kerygma is reserved for the AT
expert.explanation: C.H. Dodd has shown that the apostolic preaching of Acts and the epistles share a common kerygmatic core centered on Easter.

expert.question: What does the phrase 'inaugurated eschatology' ('already and not yet') mean to describe Jesus' teaching on the Kingdom of God?
options: That the Kingdom is only in the distant future
That the Kingdom has already erupted in the person and works of Jesus ('if it is by the finger of God...'), while awaiting its final consummation upon his return
That the Kingdom was only political in the year 30
That the resurrection has already taken place for everyone
expert.explanation: This tension between the 'already' (Mark 1:15; Luke 11:20) and the 'not yet' (Matthew 6:10; Rev 11:15) runs throughout the New Testament.

expert.question: In Romans 1:16-17, what is the meaning of the expression 'righteousness of God' (dikaiosynê theou) according to the classical reading of the Reformation and modern exegesis?
options: Both the saving righteousness that God freely grants through faith and God's righteous faithfulness to his covenant in Christ
The justice of the Roman courts
The moral merit acquired by man
expert.explanation: The gospel reveals how God remains righteous while justifying those who have faith in Jesus (Romans 3:26).

expert.question: What is the meaning of the probable pre-Pauline hymn of Philippians 2:6-11 ('in the form of God', morphê theou)?
options: Jesus was only a human appearance
Pre-existing in divine nature/condition (morphê theou), Christ did not claim equality with God as a jealous privilege, but humbled himself to the cross, receiving the name Lord (Kyrios)
Jesus became god only after his death
expert.explanation: The application of Isaiah 45:23 ('every knee shall bow') to Jesus in v.10-11 unequivocally affirms his full divinity shared with YHWH.

expert.question: In Colossians 2:14-15, what legal and military image does Paul use to describe the victory of the cross?
options: Christ has blotted out the act of which the ordinances condemned us by nailing it to the cross, and has stripped the dominions and authorities by making a public spectacle of them.
expert.explanation: The cross which seemed to be the triumph of hostile powers becomes the triumphal chariot of God exposing their defeat.

expert.question: In 1 Corinthians 15:3-5, what status do NT historians give to the phrase 'Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, he was buried, he was raised on the third day...'?
options: A late invention from the 2nd century
A primitive creed received by Paul very shortly after the crucifixion (from the years 30-35 AD)
expert.explanation: Paul uses the technical rabbinic verbs 'receive' (paralambanô) and 'transmit' (paradidômi), attesting to the antiquity of the Easter faith.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the 'new perspective on Paul' (Sanders, Dunn, Wright) in contemporary Pauline studies?
options: She maintains that 1st century Judaism was a 'covenant nomism' based on grace, and that the 'works of the law' mainly target identity markers (circumcision, Sabbath, dietary laws) excluding pagans.
Paul did not write any epistles
expert.explanation: While sparking debates with classical Reformed reading, this approach has renewed understanding of the Jewish context of Galatians and Romans.

expert.question: In Romans 7:14-25 ('I do not do the good that I want...'), what are the two main readings of the identity of the 'I' (Egô)?
options: Either man under the Law without the power of the Spirit (recent majority exegesis), or the persistent inner struggle of the regenerate Christian (Augustine, Reformation)
expert.explanation: The contrast between Romans 7 (slavery under the Law) and Romans 8 (freedom in the Spirit) informs this classic exegetical discussion.

expert.question: In Galatians 2:11-14, why does Paul publicly oppose Peter (Cephas) ​​in Antioch?
options: Because Peter, for fear of the circumcised people coming from Jerusalem, stopped eating with non-Jewish Christians, compromising 'the truth of the Gospel'
Because Peter wanted to go to Rome
For the choice of a bishop
expert.explanation: Paul shows that justification by faith alone prohibits any separation of tables between Jewish and Gentile believers.

expert.question: What is the chiasmatic or thematic literary structure of the epistle to the Hebrews?
options: A 'word of exhortation' alternating Christological presentations (superiority of Christ over the angels, Moses, Aaron and the sacrifices) and solemn warnings against apostasy
A Chronological Account of Paul's Life
A private letter to a king
expert.explanation: Hebrews combines high priestly Christology with five warning passages urging readers to persevere in the faith.

expert.question: In Hebrews 6:4-6 and 10:26, what specific danger is the author warning his recipients about?
options: Deliberate apostasy — publicly rejecting the one sacrifice of Christ and returning to the ancient rites, leaving no other sacrifice for sins
expert.explanation: In the context of persecution, some were tempted to abandon the Christian faith to find the security of Judaism recognized by Rome.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'hypostasis' (ὑπόστασις) in Hebrews 1:3 ('the imprint of one's person/substance') and 11:1 ('firm assurance')?
options: In 1:3, it designates the very being or substantial reality of God of which the Son is the exact imprint; in 11:1, the concrete assurance of the hoped-for goods
expert.explanation: Hebrews 1:3 played a decisive role in the development of the Trinitarian Christology of the early councils.

expert.question: How does the epistle of James (2:24: 'by works a man is justified, and not by faith only') harmonize with Paul (Romans 3:28)?
options: Paul fights legalism (meriting salvation before God without faith in Christ); James fights a dead and purely verbal faith (demonstrating the authenticity of his faith through works)
expert.explanation: Paul and James use 'justify' and 'faith' from two complementary angles: one speaks of the foundation of salvation, the other of its living verification.

expert.question: In 1 Peter 3:18-20, what is the most debated interpretation of Christ's preaching 'to the spirits in prison'?
options: Either the proclamation by the Spirit through Noah to the contemporaries of the flood, or the announcement of Christ's victory to the fallen powers/spirits after his death
A universal second chance after death clearly proven
A dream of Peter at Joppa
expert.explanation: The passage remains one of the most discussed texts of the NT, but its pastoral purpose is clear: to encourage persecuted Christians through the total victory of Christ (v. 22).

expert.question: In 2 Peter 3:8-10, how does the apostle respond to scoffers who doubt Christ's return ("Where is the promise of his coming?")?
options: Recalling the past flood, that before the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and that this apparent 'delay' is God's patience willing that none should perish
By denying the end of the world
Saying that the return has already taken place in secret
expert.explanation: God's patience is a missionary grace that allows time for repentance before renewal by fire.

expert.question: What is the close literary relationship between the epistle of Jude and chapter 2 of the 2nd epistle of Peter?
options: They share very similar material and images against false libertine doctors (e.g. one was probably inspired by the other or a common source)
expert.explanation: The majority of scholars believe that 2 Peter 2 adapted and reused Jude by omitting his quotations from Jewish apocrypha (1 Enoch, Assumption of Moses).

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'koinônia' (κοινωνία) in the New Testament (Acts 2:42; 2 Cor 13:13; 1 John 1:3)?
options: A deep and reciprocal communion/participation with God (Father, Son, Spirit) and between believers, involving material sharing and spiritual solidarity
expert.explanation: Koinônia expresses the sharing of new life in Christ, up to the financial collection for the poor of Jerusalem (Romans 15:26).

expert.question: In John 1:1 ('In the beginning was the Logos... and the Logos was God'), what grammatical nuance specifies the construction without article 'theos ên ho logos'?
options: That the Logos fully possesses the divine nature (qualitative) while remaining distinct from the person of the Father ('near God')
That the Logos is a simple creature
That God has ceased to exist
expert.explanation: The absence of an article before 'theos' (Colwell's rule) avoids modalism (confusing the Father and the Son) while affirming the true divinity of the Word.

expert.question: In John 1:14 ('And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us'), what Greek verb refers to the Old Testament?
options: Eskênôsen ('pitched his tent/tabernacle' among us), evoking the tent of meeting and the glory of God (Shekinah)
expert.explanation: In Jesus, the glorious presence of God which resided in the Tabernacle comes to dwell bodily in the midst of humanity.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the expression 'Born again / from above' (gennêthênai anôthen) in the dialogue with Nicodemus (John 3:3)?
options: The Greek word 'anôthen' means both 'again' and 'from above' - a double meaning used by John to designate spiritual birth from God
expert.explanation: Nicodemus only grasps the temporal meaning ('entering a second time into his mother's womb'), while Jesus speaks of a birth 'from above' by the Spirit.

expert.question: In John 19:30, what single Greek word does Jesus speak on the cross ('It is finished')?
options: Tetelestai (perfect tense of the verb teleô: fully completed, paid in full, with permanent effect)
expert.explanation: On ancient commercial receipts, 'tetelestai' meant 'paid in full'; Jesus proclaims the perfect completion of the redemptive work.

expert.question: In Luke 15, what is the common thread that unites the three parables (lost sheep, lost coin, prodigal son)?
options: The joy of God seeking and welcoming the repentant sinner—in response to the murmurings of the Pharisees and scribes (Luke 15:1-2)
expert.explanation: Each parable culminates in the call to share the joy of heaven before a single sinner who repents, calling out to the older brother (the Pharisees).

expert.question: What is the role of 'Luke's prologue' (Luke 1:1-4) in the context of Greco-Roman historiography?
options: A formal methodological dedication to Théophile affirming a rigorous investigation of eyewitnesses to guarantee the solidity of the teachings received
expert.explanation: Luke uses careful literary Greek comparable to the prefaces of ancient historians like Thucydides or Polybius.

expert.question: In Acts 15, what four abstentions does the Jerusalem Apostolic Decree agree to facilitate fellowship between Jewish and Gentile Christians?
options: The Sabbath, Circumcision, Wine and Meat
Meat sacrificed to idols, blood, strangled animals, and fornication (sexual immorality)
Commerce, the military, taxes and marriage
expert.explanation: Without imposing circumcision or the yoke of the Law for salvation, the council asks for these practical considerations in connection with Leviticus 17-18.

expert.question: In Romans 9-11, what major theological issue does Paul address after exalting the assurance of salvation in Romans 8?
options: How to pay taxes to Caesar
How to reconcile God's faithful promises to Israel with the fact that the majority of Israel rejected their Messiah
How to build a church in Rome
expert.explanation: If God's word seemed to have failed Israel, how could the believers in Rome trust Romans 8? Paul demonstrates that God's faithfulness remains intact.

expert.question: In 1 Corinthians 1-4, what is the deep root of the divisions in the Corinthian Church?
options: A disagreement over the date of Easter
Partisan attachment to leaders (Paul, Apollos, Cephas) ​​fueled by the search for 'human wisdom' and social prestige rather than the madness of the cross
expert.explanation: Paul contrasts worldly rhetoric with the 'word of the cross', the power and wisdom of God which overthrows human pride.

expert.question: In 1 Corinthians 8-10, what ethical principle does Paul formulate regarding meats sacrificed to idols?
options: Eat everything without worrying about anyone
Christian freedom (“all things are permitted, but not all things edify”) must be guided by love for the weak brother whose conscience could be wounded
Return under the Law of Moses
expert.explanation: It is not enough to know that an idol is nothing: knowledge puffs up, but love edifies (1 Corinthians 8:1).

expert.question: In 2 Corinthians 3:6 ('the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life'), what exactly does 'the letter' mean in context?
options: Any literal reading of the Bible
The old covenant written in stone (the Law without the renewed heart) which condemns the sinner, opposed to the ministry of the new covenant by the Spirit
expert.explanation: Paul does not denigrate the biblical text but compares the Sinaitic ministry of condemnation with the ministry of justification by the Spirit.

expert.question: In Ephesians 1:3-14, what is the grammatical and theological feature of the opening passage?
options: It is a single long sentence (eulogy) in Greek of 202 words blessing God according to a trinitarian structure (election by the Father, redemption by the Son, seal by the Spirit)
expert.explanation: Each section of this blessing culminates in the refrain 'in praise of the glory of his grace' / 'in praise of his glory'.

expert.question: In Ephesians 5:21-33, how does Paul establish the ethics of Christian marriage?
options: On the Roman laws of patria potestas
On the 'great mystery' of the union between Christ and the Church: the husband called to love his wife as Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her
expert.explanation: Preceded by 'submit to one another in the fear of Christ' (v. 21), the text radically transforms ancient family codes through sacrificial love.

expert.question: In 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18, why does Paul write about the resurrection and the rapture?
options: To comfort believers worried about their brothers who died before the Lord's return, assuring that they will not be disadvantaged
To fix the year 60 AD. AD
expert.explanation: 'Therefore comfort one another with these words' (v. 18): first the dead in Christ will be raised, and then all will be with the Lord forever.

expert.question: In 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1, what interchangeable terms refer to local leaders of the apostolic Church?
options: Presbyters/elders (presbyteroi) and bishops/overseers (episkopoi), assisted by deacons (diakonoi)
expert.explanation: In Titus 1:5-7 and Acts 20:17,28, 'elder' and 'bishop/overseer' again designate the same collegial function of pastoral leadership.

expert.question: In Titus 2:11-14, how does Paul summarize the connection between appeared grace, present ethics, and future hope?
options: Saving grace 'teaches us to renounce impiety... and to live in this present age according to wisdom, justice and piety, while awaiting the blessed hope'
Grace is only for the old
expert.explanation: Divine grace is both a source of forgiveness (first appearance) and a pedagogy of holiness until the glorious appearance of Christ.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the Greek word 'anathema' used by Paul in Galatians 1:8-9 and Romans 9:3?
options: That which is doomed to execration or curse/separation from God (equivalent to the 'herem' of the LXX)
