expert.explanation: Paul declares anathema to anyone who preaches any other gospel than that of grace, and expresses in Romans 9:3 his extreme love for Israel.

expert.question: In Romans 16:7, who are Andronicus and Junia mentioned by Paul with the notable title of 'regarded among the apostles'?
options: A couple (including Junia, female first name) converted before Paul and esteemed among the apostles/sent ones
Two enemies of Paul in Ephesus
expert.explanation: The Fathers of the Church (including John Chrysostom) recognized Junia as a remarkable woman in the wider circle of apostles/missionaries.

expert.question: In 2 Corinthians 8–9, what spiritual principles does Paul teach about collecting for the saints in Jerusalem?
options: Voluntary, joyful generosity ('God loves those who give with joy'), proportional to means, as a sign of spiritual and material reciprocity
Give to buy positions of authority
expert.explanation: Paul bases this liberality on the grace of Christ who, 'even though he was rich, he became poor for you, so that through his poverty you might be enriched' (2 Cor 8:9).

expert.question: In Revelation, what does the constantly repeated number '7' mean (7 Churches, 7 spirits, 7 seals, 7 trumpets, 7 bowls)?
options: The biblical symbol of divine fullness, totality and perfection
The number of years of Nero's reign
expert.explanation: Thus the 'seven Churches' represent both historical communities of Asia Minor and the universal Church in its entirety.

expert.question: In Revelation, how can we interpret the '1000 years' (Revelation 20) according to amillennialism, premillennialism and postmillennialism?
options: They all say the same thing

Amillennialism: the present era of the Church between the 1st and 2nd coming; Premillennialism: earthly reign of 1000 years after the return of Christ; Postmillennialism: golden age of the Gospel before the return
The text speaks of only 1000 days
No one comments on this chapter
expert.explanation: These three schools share the common faith in the personal return of Christ, the general resurrection and the final judgment.

expert.question: In Revelation 13:18, what does the number '666' (man's number) represent according to the most common ancient gematria?
options: The triple imperfection (below the divine 7) and, for many historians, the Hebrew numerical value of 'Neron Qesar' (Nero Caesar)
expert.explanation: In Hebrew, the letters of 'Neron Qesar' total 666 (and 616 with 'Nero Qesar' without the final 'n', a variant attested in certain manuscripts).

expert.question: In Revelation 21-22, why is there 'no temple' in the New Jerusalem?
options: 'For the Lord God Almighty is his temple, and the Lamb' — symbolic mediation gives way to direct communion
Because the temple remains in Rome
expert.explanation: The entire city takes the cubic form of the Holy of Holies (21:16), signifying that all of the renewed creation becomes the immediate home of God.

expert.question: In John 17:20-23, what is the missionary significance of Jesus' prayer for the unity of believers?
options: May all be one as the Father and the Son are one, 'that the world may believe that you have sent me'
A retreat far from the world
A merger with the Roman Empire
expert.explanation: The spiritual unity visible in the love between disciples constitutes the most powerful testimony to the divine origin of Christ.

expert.question: In Matthew 16:18-19, what does the phrase 'the gates of hell (Hades) shall not prevail against it' mean?
options: That the Church will physically attack cemeteries
The gates represent the fortresses of death and evil: they will not be able to resist the advance of the Church nor hold its members in death
expert.explanation: In ancient times, gates were defensive structures: the Church built by Christ besieged and defeated the kingdom of death.

expert.question: In Luke 16:19–31 (the rich man and Lazarus), what conclusion does Abraham draw about the sufficiency of Scripture?
options: That a resurrected person will always convince everyone
'If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone from the dead rises'
expert.explanation: The parable shows the irreversibility of judgment after death and that true faith is born from listening to the Word of God.

expert.question: In Matthew 12:31-32, what is 'blasphemy against the Holy Spirit' in its immediate context?
options: The lucid and persistent hardness of the Pharisees knowingly attributing to Beelzebub (Satan) the manifest works of the Spirit of God accomplished by Jesus
expert.explanation: He who deliberately rejects the very source of light and forgiveness by calling it demonic voluntarily closes himself to repentance.

expert.question: In Acts 2:42, what are the four pillars of the life of the early church in Jerusalem?
options: The teaching of the apostles, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayers
Animal sacrifices, pilgrimages to Rome, annual fasting and philosophy
expert.explanation: These four regular practices formed the spiritual and community rhythm of the first believers.

expert.question: In 1 John 2:1-2, how does John articulate the call not to sin and the hope in case of falling?
options: If anyone sins, all is lost
'I write these things to you so that you may not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an Advocate (Paraclete) with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous'
expert.explanation: Jesus Christ is both our Advocate with the Father and the propitiation victim (hilasmos) for our sins and those of the whole world.

expert.question: In Romans 6:1-14, why does Paul reject the idea of ​​'remaining in sin so that grace may abound'?
options: Because through baptism and union with Christ, the believer is dead to sin and resurrected to walk in newness of life
Because the Law of Moses still saves
expert.explanation: Grace does not set free to sin, but sets free from the bondage of sin to serve righteousness.

expert.question: In 1 Peter 1:3-5, how does Peter describe the Christian hope and its heritage?
options: A living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, for an inheritance that cannot be corrupted, nor defiled, nor withered, reserved in heaven
expert.explanation: Believers are kept by the power of God through faith for that salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

expert.question: In Matthew 13, what is the common lesson of the parables of the 'mustard seed' and the 'leaven'?
options: Although the beginnings of the Kingdom of God seem tiny and hidden, its growth is irresistible until it transforms and encompasses all creation
expert.explanation: Jesus thus reassures his disciples in the face of the apparent modesty of their group in the face of great empires.

expert.question: In John 10:11-18, what characteristics distinguish the 'Good Shepherd' from the 'mercenary'?
options: The mercenary flees when the wolf comes because he does not care for the sheep; the Good Shepherd knows his own, calls them by name and gives his life for them
The Good Shepherd abandons the weak sheep
expert.explanation: Jesus clarifies that he gives his life voluntarily (“No one takes it from me, but I give it of myself”) and that he still has other sheep (the nations) to gather.

expert.question: In Luke 19:11-27, why does Jesus tell the parable of the ten minas just before entering Jerusalem?
options: Because it was believed that the Kingdom of God would appear immediately; it shows that the King must leave to receive royalty before returning to ask his servants for an account
expert.explanation: The parable prepares the disciples for a period of active waiting and faithfulness between the Ascension and the return of Christ.

expert.question: In 2 Timothy 3:16-17, what does the Greek term 'theopneustos' ('breathed by God') mean?
options: 'God-breathed' — affirming the divine origin of the Scriptures which makes them fully sufficient for teaching, convicting, correcting and instructing
expert.explanation: God breathed His Word through human authors (2 Peter 1:21) that the man of God might be complete, equipped for every good work.

expert.question: In Philippians 1:21-24, what inner dilemma does Paul express as he faces his trial in Rome?
options: Between the desire to depart and be with Christ (which is by far the best) and the need to remain in the flesh for the spiritual progress of the Philippians
To become a Roman citizen or not
expert.explanation: This passage attests to Paul's hope of being immediately with Christ upon death, while remaining devoted to the service of the Church.

expert.question: In Acts 20:28, what strong expression does Paul use before the elders of Ephesus to describe the value of the Church?
options: 'The Church of God, which he purchased with his own blood'
expert.explanation: Paul entrusts the elders with the care of this precious flock purchased at the price of the very blood of Christ.

expert.question: In Revelation 12:1-17, who symbolically represent the Woman clothed with the sun, the Male Child and the Red Dragon?
options: God's faithful people (Israel/Church) giving birth to the Messiah (delighted with God), and Satan defeated who then pursues the rest of his descendants
expert.explanation: The chapter reveals the invisible spiritual background of earthly persecutions: the dragon is already defeated by the blood of the Lamb (v. 11).
